1_G3.question: WP5 gate G3 fails on repair_v8 only through its no-A/C-regression clause (A-PARSEC alpha 2.0 at R_V 3.0 and 3.1). Does the clause apply to a data-defect fix?
1_G3.decision: The clause applies as written. G3 stays recorded as FAILED on repair_v8, with the explanation that the two pass->fail cells compare against a predecessor computed on defective anchor masses. repair_v8 remains adopted (its adoption never depended on G3).
1_G3.note: both regressed cells are alpha = 2.0, which decision 2 removes from the headline

2_alpha_headline.question: The headline set alpha in {2.0, 2.3} keeps a slope that fits no better than the one it drops.
2_alpha_headline.decision: NEW HEADLINE RULE: alpha = 2.3 is the headline slope. alpha = 2.0 and 2.6 are reported as sensitivity branches (never deleted, shown alongside). Supersedes the 36-branch alpha in {2.0, 2.3} headline set of WP7 D1 (wp7_alpha_headline_adoption_outcome_*).

justification.reading: E1 alone rejects neither extreme (p ~ 0.07 each vs ~0.2); E2, the held-back out-of-sample check, separates them strongly in favour of 2.3.
caveats: issue #15 (unmodelled massive-star multiplicity) can shift E2
C alone prefers 2.0 on E1 and E2; C's age is under test (issue #20 Phase A')
